title: Former RAAF Member Describes Hypnosis-Recalled UAP Encounter
excerpt: Troy Gavin told investigative journalist Ross Coulthart about beings he recalled under hypnotic regression, in an interview released on 24 November 2026.
content:
Troy Gavin, identified by NewsNation as a former Royal Australian Air Force member, described an alleged unidentified aerial phenomenon encounter he recalled through hypnotic regression years after a teenage camping trip. The account was released in an interview with Ross Coulthart as part of his investigation into UAP at Barwon Heads in southern Victoria.

Why it matters

A 2025 research review in the International Journal of Clinical and Experimental Hypnosis found hypnosis did not improve accurate recollection and in some cases hindered it. IBTimes UK cannot independently verify whether the events Gavin described occurred, and NASA states there is no evidence of an extraterrestrial origin for UAP.

The account rests on hypnotic regression, a method a 2025 research review found did not improve accurate recollection. Gavin's claims are unverified, and no independent evidence of the encounter has been published.

The players

Troy Gavin

Troy Gavin is a former Royal Australian Air Force member who is also identified by NewsNation as a principal at White Hawk Psionics.

Ross Coulthart

Ross Coulthart is an investigative journalist known for his reporting on unidentified aerial phenomena.

NASA

NASA is the United States national aeronautics and space agency, which states there is no evidence of an extraterrestrial origin for UAP.

The details

Gavin said he recalled beings he described as 'tall, grey, large eyes, long arms, long fingers.' He reportedly became lost with friends during a teenage camping trip before encountering a powerful, silent light, and his recollections surfaced years later through hypnotic regression.

Timeline

  1. During Gavin's teenage years, he and friends reportedly became lost on a camping trip and saw a light.

  2. Years after the camping incident, Gavin underwent hypnotic regression.

  3. In 2025, a research review found hypnosis did not improve accurate recall.

  4. On 24 November 2026, an interview with Ross Coulthart was released.

Roadmap

NASA states there is no evidence of an extraterrestrial origin for UAP, placing Gavin's hypnosis-recalled account against the agency's documented position. The claim adds a personal testimony to a debate that official scientific bodies have so far addressed through evidence rather than individual recollection.

Readers weighing claims of this kind should note that hypnotic recall is not considered reliable evidence of past events. Treat individual accounts as unverified until supported by independent documentation.

The takeaway

Personal testimony recovered under hypnosis is not reliable evidence on its own. Readers should weigh such accounts against independent verification and the research on recall.
